key_insight: Models handle many calculations and physical explanations well but struggle to distinguish similar material states and make quantitatively supported decisions.
engineering_relevance: Reliable AI-assisted materials discovery requires condition-specific reasoning and evidence updates that improve predictions without destabilizing accurate ones.
method: M1: Test unaided, condition-specific reasoning across ten research functions.
M2: Evaluate agent-assisted transfer of related knowledge to unresolved materials questions.
MatEvoBench-20: Assess initial forecasts and revisions as experimental observations accumulate.
evidence_signal: Across eleven model deployments, M1's 200 aluminium and high-entropy alloy tasks and complementary evaluations reveal weaker fine-grained estimates, state comparisons and quantitative choices.
watch_item: Literature transfer can fail when conditions or baselines differ, and new observations can destabilize previously accurate predictions.
paper_title: Benchmarking language models and agents for scientific reasoning in evolving materials laboratories
